h: Old Town Horrors on Your Doorstep
p: The Dungeon sits on Market Street, tucked below the Old Town and right by Waverley Station, which makes it about as easy to reach as anything in the city. Arriving by train? You can be out of the station and into the gloom in a matter of minutes. From there, the steep closes and steps leading up to the Royal Mile are right on hand, and Princes Street Gardens and the Scott Monument are just over the tracks.

If the Dungeon whets your appetite for the city's grimmer side, Edinburgh has plenty more where that came from. The Real Mary King's Close takes you into the hidden streets buried beneath the Royal Mile, and the city has no shortage of evening ghost tours wandering the Old Town once the light fades. On the other hand, if you need something calmer to balance out the screams, the National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street is free to enter and packed with everything from dinosaurs to Dolly the sheep.

A few tips: arrive a little early for your slot, wear sensible shoes for the cobbles outside and the shuffling inside, and keep bags small. Summer and the August festival season get very busy in this part of town, so leave a bit of breathing space in your plans for crowds and queues.
